CARLOS1ING.name: Charles I of England
CARLOS1ING.summary: Stuart king of England, Scotland and Ireland. His confrontation with Parliament led to the English Civil Wars and ended with his execution in 1649.
sections: The son of James VI and I and Anne of Denmark, he was born at Dunfermline in 1600 and reigned over England, Scotland and Ireland from 1625. His marriage to the Catholic Henrietta Maria of France and his trust in the Duke of Buckingham aroused suspicion.

After the Petition of Right (1628), he dissolved Parliament and ruled without summoning it between 1629 and 1640, relying on contested taxes such as ship money. His attempt to impose an Anglican liturgy in Scotland provoked the Bishops’ Wars and forced him to summon Parliament again.

The confrontation with the Long Parliament led to civil war in 1642. Defeated at Naseby (1645), he negotiated with the Scots and Parliamentarians while encouraging a second war. Cromwell’s army brought him to trial for treason, and he was beheaded at Whitehall in January 1649; the monarchy was abolished until 1660.

EUGENIOSABOYA.name: Eugene of Savoy
EUGENIOSABOYA.summary: A prince of the house of Savoy-Carignano raised at the court of Louis XIV, he entered Habsburg service in 1683 and became the Empire’s leading general. He defeated the Ottomans at Zenta (1697) and Belgrade (1717) and, alongside Marlborough, defeated France at Blenheim, Oudenarde and Malplaquet during the War of the Spanish Succession.
sections: A prince with no place at Versailles

He was born in Paris in 1663, the youngest of the five sons of Eugene Maurice of Savoy-Carignano, Count of Soissons, and Olympia Mancini, a niece of Mazarin. His mother fell from favour and fled France in 1680 after the Affair of the Poisons. Intended for the Church, Eugene asked Louis XIV for a military command, but the king refused because of his appearance and his family.

In 1683 he travelled to Vienna, then under Ottoman siege, and entered the army of Leopold I. He fought in the reconquest of Buda (1686) and in the Hungarian campaigns. In 1697 he received supreme command and defeated the army of Sultan Mustafa II at Zenta, a victory that prepared the Peace of Karlowitz (1699), through which the Habsburgs gained almost all of Hungary and Transylvania.
The War of the Spanish Succession

President of the Imperial War Council from 1703, he joined the Duke of Marlborough in defeating the French and Bavarians at Blenheim (1704). In 1706 he lifted the siege of Turin, driving the French from northern Italy, and later governed the State of Milan. With Marlborough he won again at Oudenarde (1708) and Malplaquet (1709), and he negotiated the Peace of Rastatt (1714) with Marshal Villars.

In a new war against the Ottomans he won at Petrovaradin (1716) and captured Belgrade in 1717. From 1716 to 1724 he was governor-general of the Austrian Netherlands, which he administered from Vienna. He supported Charles VI’s Pragmatic Sanction, assembled a great library and art collections, and built the Belvedere Palace. He died unmarried in Vienna in 1736.

Daughter of Valdemar IV and sister of Margarita. Her marriage to Enrique de Mecklenburg linked the Danish house to a family that also claimed rights in Sweden. Through her daughter Mary was the grandmother of Erik of Pomerania: this is the family connection that made it possible to promote her by Margarita.

conyuges.resumen: A duke of the Griffin dynasty, he belonged to the Pomeranian branches that connected the Baltic with neighbouring monarchies. His marriage to Marie of Mecklenburg made him the father of Erik of Pomerania and Catherine.
conyuges.biografia: A duke of the Griffin dynasty, he belonged to the Pomeranian branches that connected the Baltic with neighbouring monarchies. His marriage to Marie of Mecklenburg made him the father of Erik of Pomerania and Catherine. His descendants later reached the Scandinavian crowns without making Pomerania part of the Kalmar Union.

hijos.resumen: The grandson of Margarita was promoted as heir and recognized in the three kingdoms before the coronation of Kalmar in 1397. Margarita continued to run the policy until 1412.

Erik’s sister from Pomerania. She married John of the Palatinate-Neumarkt, from the house of Wittelsbach. Her son Christopher was elected in the three Nordic kingdoms after Erik’s fall. Filiation shows family continuity, although Christopher’s access depended on separate choices.

relacionadosDinastia.resumen: Alberto de Mecklenburg, king of Sweden since 1364 with the support of the Swedish nobility. His conflict with Margarita I ended with his defeat in Åsle (1389).
Duke of Mecklenburg, 1348–1379. Duke of the Mecklenburg dynasty.
Duke of Mecklenburg, 1422–1477. Duke of the Mecklenburg dynasty.
Duke of Mecklenburg, 1477–1503. Duke of the House of Mecklenburg.
Consort of the Mecklenburg dynasty. Their career was connected to Saxony.
Duke of Mecklenburg, 1503–1552 (Branch rule). Duke of the Mecklenburg dynasty.

contemporaneos.resumen: Alberto de Mecklenburg, king of Sweden since 1364 with the support of the Swedish nobility. His conflict with Margarita I ended with his defeat in Åsle (1389).
Duke of Mecklenburg, 1348–1379. Duke of the Mecklenburg dynasty.

Sister of Magnus Eriksson and daughter of Ingeborg of Norway. She married Albert II of Mecklenburg. Her son Albert was king of Sweden, while the offspring of her son Henry led to Erik of Pomerania. It is a key connection between Bjälbo, Mecklenburg and the Kalmar union.

Emperor of the house of Luxembourg and king of Bohemia, became Prague one of the great political and cultural centers of Europe. The Gold Bullet of 1356 ordered the imperial election in a lasting way.

King of Aragon and Navarra, central figure of the dynastic conflicts of the Iberian peninsula of the 15th century. He was the father of Fernando the Catholic and key piece in the expansion of the Statámara.
The Caspe Commitment chose it to succeed Martin I, opening the Aragon Trastamara branch. He had previously exercised the regency of Castile during the minority of John II.

DAVID1KAKH.name: David I of Kakheti
DAVID1KAKH.summary: He deposed his father Alexander II and occupied the throne for about a year. His death allowed Alexander to return. Through his wife Ketevan and son Teimuraz, his line became associated with resistance to Abbas I.

translatedSource.resumen: He deposed his father Alexander II and occupied the throne for about a year. His death allowed Alexander to return. Through his wife Ketevan and son Teimuraz, his line became associated with resistance to Abbas I.
translatedSource.biografia: He deposed his father Alexander II and occupied the throne for about a year. His death allowed Alexander to return. Through his wife Ketevan and son Teimuraz, his line became associated with resistance to Abbas I.

padres.resumen: He sought Russian protection without completely breaking up with Persia. His son David briefly removed him from power; after he had recovered him, he died in another family coup led by Constantine. The two stages of his reign are separate.

conyuges.resumen: Widow of David I, defended the rights of her son Teimuraz and intervened in the Kakhetin government. She was held hostage in Persia and was executed after refusing to convert to Islam. Her religious memory transcended Georgia through missionary testimonies.

hijos.resumen: Poet and king, he alternated resistance, negotiation and exile in the face of the pressure of Abbas I and his successors. The 1625 rebellion allowed him to return and extend his authority to Kartli, but Rostom eventually moved him. His family suffered captivity, executions and displacements.

relacionadosDinastia.resumen: Raised in Persia, he had his father Alexander II killed, but his rule provoked a rebellion led by Ketevan and he died before consolidating his power. His case shows the limits of Safavid intervention in the succession.

He took over the government after his father Simon was captured by the Ottomans. He cooperated with Abbas I against them and tried to open contacts with Russia. His offspring connects the succession of Kartli with the court of Teimuraz I of Kakheti.

The daughter of Levan of Kakheti and wife of Simon I of Kartli. Her family linked the two Eastern monarchies through their children and grandchildren; these marriages coexisted with political rivalries and with the intervention of Persia and the Ottomans.

He came to the throne as a teenager and had to face family rebellions and intervention from the neighboring principalities. He was deposed and died captive, leaving open the struggle for control of the Western monarchy.

Raised in the Persian court environment, he was installed by Abbas I after the fall of Luarsab II. His authority depended on the safavid presence and was limited outside the centers that he controlled.
He depended on Mingrelia's backing to attain and regain the throne. His reign included a break during the intervention of Simon of Kartli and his Western rivals, so two mandates are recorded.

contemporaneos.resumen: His career in the Safavid administration preceded a long reign in Kartli. He combined loyalty to the shah with agreements with local nobles and protection of Christian institutions. After defeating Teimuraz, he extended his authority into Kakheti and arranged a succession by adoption.

He restored the Kakheti monarchy after the occupation of Kartli. His long reign sought stability through agreements with Persia and contacts with Russia. The marriages of his children linked Kakheti to the other houses in the Caucasus.

Raised in Persia, he had his father Alexander II killed, but his rule provoked a rebellion led by Ketevan and he died before consolidating his power. His case shows the limits of Safavid intervention in the succession.

Daughter of George X of Kartli and wife of Teimuraz I of Kakheti. The marriage strengthened cooperation between the two branches during their wars against Persia. Her children linked this generation to the later kings of Kakheti and Imereti.

The daughter of Levan of Kakheti and wife of Simon I of Kartli. Her family linked the two Eastern monarchies through their children and grandchildren; these marriages coexisted with political rivalries and with the intervention of Persia and the Ottomans.

aliases: Enrique IV de Francia y III de Navarra
contemporaneos.resumen: First King Bourbon of France and former King of Navarra. It ended much of the French religious wars and rebuilt the monarchical authority after decades of conflict.

AMEDEO7SAB.name: Amadeus VII of Savoy
AMEDEO7SAB.summary: The Red Count succeeded his father Amadeo VI and maintained the relationship with the French monarchy. He married Bona of Berry and was the father of Amadeo VIII. His early death left a child heir and opened a struggle for regency between the mother and the new count's grandmother.

translatedSource.resumen: The Red Count succeeded his father Amadeo VI and maintained the relationship with the French monarchy. He married Bona of Berry and was the father of Amadeo VIII. His early death left a child heir and opened a struggle for regency between the mother and the new count's grandmother.
translatedSource.biografia: The Red Count succeeded his father Amadeo VI and maintained the relationship with the French monarchy. He married Bona of Berry and was the father of Amadeo VIII. fuentes.titulo: Deutsche Nationalbibliothek · Ficha de autoridad GND · Amadeus VII., Savoyen, Graf

padres.resumen: Known as the Green Count, he belonged to the generation that strengthened Savoy’s political and military reach. He was the son of Aymon and Yolanda of Montferrat, bringing together Savoyard and Palaiologan ancestry.
Consort of the Bourbon dynasty. Their career was connected to Bourbon and Savoy.

conyuges.resumen: Consort of the Valois dynasty. Their career was connected to France and Savoy.

hijos.resumen: He inherited as a child and became the first Duke of Savoy in 1416. The elevation in rank did not create a new dynasty.

hijos.nombre: Joanna of Savoy, Marchioness of Montferrat
hijos.resumen: Daughter of Amadeus VII and Bona de Berry, she married Juan James of Montferrat. She was the mother of William VIII, Bonifacio III and Isabel, wife of Ludovico I of Saluzzo.

relacionadosDinastia.resumen: Consort of the Savoy dynasty. Their career was connected to Milan.
Daughter of Amadeus V of Savoy and wife of Andronikos III Paleologist. She was regent by her son John V during the civil war against Juan Cantacuceno (1341-1347).

A younger son of Amadeus V, he inherited after his brother Edward, whose daughter also asserted succession rights. His marriage to Yolande of Montferrat linked the House of Savoy to the new Italian branch of the Palaiologoi.
relacionadosDinastia.biografia: A younger son of Amadeus V, he inherited after his brother Edward, whose daughter also asserted succession rights. His marriage to Yolande of Montferrat linked the House of Savoy to the new Italian branch of the Palaiologoi. He was the father of Amadeus VI and Blanche, through whom the family became connected with the Visconti of Milan.

relacionadosDinastia.resumen: The son of Amadeus VIII and Mary of Burgundy, he assumed government functions before becoming Duke. His marriage to Anna of Lusignan linked Savoy to Cyprus.
Count of Savoy, 1323–1329. Count of the Savoy dynasty.
Duke of Savoy from 1465, in fragile health because of epilepsy. His wife Yolande of France exercised government in practice. He was beatified for his piety.

contemporaneos.resumen: Daughter of Amadeus V of Savoy and wife of Andronikos III Paleologist. She was regent by her son John V during the civil war against Juan Cantacuceno (1341-1347).
A consort of House Valois-Borgoña whose life was connected with Burgundy, Savoy.

Emperor of the house of Luxembourg and king of Bohemia, became Prague one of the great political and cultural centers of Europe. The Gold Bullet of 1356 ordered the imperial election in a lasting way.
The Caspe Commitment chose it to succeed Martin I, opening the Aragon Trastamara branch. He had previously exercised the regency of Castile during the minority of John II.
First king of the house of Trastámara in Castile. He reached the throne after a civil war against Peter I and founded a new dynasty to dominate much of the Iberian politics of the 15th century.
He reintegrated Mallorca into his domains and fought Pedro I of Castilla. His reign reinforced the ceremonial regio and left an important autobiographical chronicle.

BOGDAN3MOLD.name: Bogdan III of Moldova
BOGDAN3MOLD.summary: Voivode of Moldavia, 1504–1517. Prince of the Bogdan-Mușat dynasty.

translatedSource.resumen: Voivode of Moldavia, 1504–1517. Prince of the Bogdan-Mușat dynasty.
translatedSource.biografia: Voivode of Moldavia, 1504–1517. Prince of the Bogdan-Mușat dynasty.

fuentes.titulo: Deutsche Nationalbibliothek · Ficha de autoridad GND · Bogdan III., Moldau, Fürst

padres.resumen: Prince of Moldavia for almost half a century and one of the central figures of fifteenth-century eastern Europe. He defended his principality against the Ottomans, Poles and Hungarians and became associated with an energetic military and religious policy.
Consort of the Basarab dynasty. Their career was connected to Wallachia, Moldova.

relacionadosDinastia.resumen: Prince of Moldova and son of Stephen the Great. He tried to maintain an active policy between Poland, Hungary and the Ottoman Empire during a time when Moldovan autonomy was increasingly difficult to sustain.
He ruled Moldova in two stages, separated by a deposition. His marriage to Ruxandra Rareș strengthened the links with the offspring of Petru Rareș.
A son of Alexandru Lăpușneanu and Ruxandra Rareș, he acceded during his minority, with his mother serving as regent until 1570.
relacionadosDinastia.biografia: A son of Alexandru Lăpușneanu and Ruxandra Rareș, he acceded during his minority, with his mother serving as regent until 1570. Relations with Poland and internal conflicts shaped his position towards the Ottomans. He lost power in 1572; kinship had not guaranteed a stable succession.

relacionadosDinastia.resumen: The daughter of Petru Rareș and Elena Branković, she married Alejandro Lăpușneanu. She intervened in the continuity of her family and, after the removal and death of her husband, exercised the regency of Bogdan IV. Her ancestry links the Moldovan sovereigns with the family of the Serbian despots.

muer.nota: She is still recorded as alive after June 1587. That reference is not converted into a definite year of death.

notas.texto: Her mother was Maria, first wife of Petru Rareș, still with no information. Elena Branković was his stepmother.

relacionadosDinastia.resumen: Daughter of Petru Rareș and her first wife Maria, she married Mircea Ciobanul. After her husband’s death she directed the government of her son Petru. Her deposition in 1568 drove the family into exile. She is still recorded in 1587, but the precise year of her death is unknown.
Voivode of Moldova, 1449–1451. Prince of the Bogdan-Mușat dynasty.

contemporaneos.resumen: A daughter of Jovan Branković and wife of Petru Rareș, she brought a connection with the Serbian despots to Moldavia. She took part in government during her son Stephen’s minority. Her daughter Ruxandra also became a Moldavian consort and regent; Chiajna, Petru’s daughter by another union, was her stepdaughter.

Prince of Moldova and son of Stephen the Great. He tried to maintain an active policy between Poland, Hungary and the Ottoman Empire during a time when Moldovan autonomy was increasingly difficult to sustain.
He ruled Moldova in two stages, separated by a deposition. His marriage to Ruxandra Rareș strengthened the links with the offspring of Petru Rareș.
A son of Alexandru Lăpușneanu and Ruxandra Rareș, he acceded during his minority, with his mother serving as regent until 1570.
contemporaneos.biografia: A son of Alexandru Lăpușneanu and Ruxandra Rareș, he acceded during his minority, with his mother serving as regent until 1570. Relations with Poland and internal conflicts shaped his position towards the Ottomans. He lost power in 1572; kinship had not guaranteed a stable succession.

contemporaneos.resumen: Emperor of the Holy Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that reached the Iberian peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. From Philip I he inherited the County of Burgundy, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. He then incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groninga and Güeldres in a step-by-step manner between 1524 and 1543. He preserved the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the duchy incorporated into France. Since 1535, Milan has been under imperial control; Philip II's invasion and subsequent possession must be distinguished from that government.

contemporaneos.nombre: Ferdinand I of the Holy Roman Empire
contemporaneos.resumen: Brother of Charles V and founder of the Austrian branch of the Habsburg. He brought together Austria, Bohemia and a large part of Hungary and finally succeeded his brother in imperial dignity.

SANCHACASTNAV.name: Sancha of Castile
SANCHACASTNAV.summary: Consort of the Ivrea-Burgundy dynasty. Their career was connected to Navarre and Castile.

translatedSource.resumen: Consort of the Ivrea-Burgundy dynasty. Their career was connected to Navarre and Castile.
translatedSource.biografia: Consort of the Ivrea-Burgundy dynasty. Their career was connected to Navarre and Castile.

fuentes.titulo: Real Academia de la Historia · Diccionario Biográfico español

conyuges.resumen: King of Navarre during the second half of the twelfth century and the father of Sancho VII and Blanche of Navarre. His family connected the kingdom with Castile and Champagne. Blanche’s descendants were decisive in the succession of 1234, when the crown passed to Theobald I.

hijos.resumen: King of Navarre, famous for his participation at Las Navas de Tolosa. His long reign closed the direct male line of Navarre’s Jiménez dynasty.

Daughter of Sancho VI and sister of Sancho VII, she married Teobaldo III of Champagne. After widowing she held the position of her son Teobaldo during her minority. For her, that son gathered a Navarrese hereditary right that became effective when her uncle Sancho VII died.

notas.texto: Married to Richard I in Limassol (Cyprus) in 1191, during the third crusade. She is the only queen of England who never stepped on the kingdom; widow, she resided in Le Mans, who received as part of her dowry.

hijos.resumen: Daughter of Sancho VI of Navarre, she married Ricardo I in Limassol (Cyprus) in 1191, during the crusade. She never lived in England; after widowing she lived in Le Mans, which was part of her dowry, and there she founded the Abbey of L’Épau, where she is buried.

relacionadosDinastia.resumen: Consort of the Ivrea-Borgoña dynasty. Their career was connected to Aragon, Castile.
King of Castile during Christian expansion into southern Iberia. After his defeat at Alarcos, victory at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212 decisively strengthened Castile’s position.
King of León for more than four decades. He convened the Cortes of 1188, and his dynastic policy made possible the permanent union of León and Castile through Ferdinand III.
He inherited Castile as a child and his minority was under the influence of the Lara. His accidental death allowed the succession of Berenguela and, through it, of Fernando III.
Queen of Castile for a short period and essential piece of dynastic continuity. He resigned in favour of his son Fernando III and retained considerable political influence during his reign.
Queen consort and regent of France, and a daughter of Alfonso VIII of Castile. She governed during Louis IX’s minority and absences and firmly defended the authority of the Capetian monarchy.

contemporaneos.resumen: King of Castile during Christian expansion into southern Iberia. After his defeat at Alarcos, victory at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212 decisively strengthened Castile’s position.
Consort of the Ivrea-Borgoña dynasty. Their career was connected to Aragon, Castile.
Consort of the Plantagenet dynasty. Their career was connected to Castile and England.

King Plantagenet who built an extensive Anglo-French rule and strengthened the law justice in England. His conflict with Thomas Becket and the rivalry between his children marked the end of his reign.
contemporaneos.titulo: King · Duke of Normandy and Aquitaine · Count of Anjou

contemporaneos.resumen: King of England whose reign was marked by the loss of much of the continental domains of the Plantagenet and the crisis that led to the Magna Charter of 1215.

The third son of Henry II and Leonor of Aquitaine, he was Duke of Aquitaine from 1172 and king of England from 1189 to 1199. He led the third crusade with Philip Augustus, defeated Saladino in Arsuf (1191) and negotiated the access of pilgrims to Jerusalem. Captured on his return by Leopoldo V from Austria, he passed to the Emperor Henry VI until he paid a huge ransom in 1194. He spent his last years defending Normandy in front of France and died in the siege of Châlus.
contemporaneos.titulo: King · Duke of Normandy and Aquitaine · Count of Anjou

BEATPORTVISEU.name: Beatrice of Portugal
aliases: Beatriz de Portugal, duquesa de Viseu
BEATPORTVISEU.summary: A daughter of Infante John and granddaughter of John I, she married her cousin Ferdinand, Duke of Viseu. Widowed in 1470, she governed the Duchy of Beja and was the mother of Manuel I and Queen Eleanor; she died at Beja in 1506.

aliases: Beatriz de Portugal, duquesa de Viseu
translatedSource.resumen: A daughter of Infante John and granddaughter of John I, she married her cousin Ferdinand, Duke of Viseu. Widowed in 1470, she governed the Duchy of Beja and was the mother of Manuel I and Queen Eleanor; she died at Beja in 1506.
translatedSource.biografia: A daughter of Infante John and granddaughter of John I, she married her cousin Ferdinand, Duke of Viseu. Widowed in 1470, she governed the Duchy of Beja and was the mother of Manuel I and Queen Eleanor; she died at Beja in 1506.

padres.resumen: Constable of the Avis dynasty. Their career was connected to Portugal.
Noble of the Braganza dynasty. Their career was connected to Portugal.

aliases: Fernando de Portugal, duque de Viseu
conyuges.resumen: Son of King Duarte, he was Duke of Viseu and Beja and heir of the throne during the minority of his brother Alfonso V. Married to his cousin Beatriz, he died in Setúbal in 1470; his younger son reigned as Manuel I.

hijos.resumen: Consort of the House of Aviz. Their life was connected with Portugal.
King of Portugal during the great cycle of ocean expansion. Under his reign, Portuguese routes to India, Africa and Brazil and Lisbon became a great imperial center.
Noble of the Aviz-Beja dynasty. Their life was connected with Portugal.

relacionadosDinastia.resumen: Daughter of Infante John of Portugal, she became John II of Castile’s second wife in 1447 and was the mother of Isabella the Catholic and Infante Alfonso. Widowed in 1454, she lived in retirement at Arévalo until her death in 1496.
King of Portugal who strengthened monarchical authority against high nobility and continued Atlantic expansion. His reign prepared the great ultra-amarine leap of Manuel I.
Consort of the House of Aviz. Their life was connected with Castile, Portugal.
King of Portugal involved in North African campaigns and in the dispute for the Spanish succession. His marriage to Juana la Beltraneja led him to face Isabel I and Fernando politically.
Prince of the Avis dynasty. Their career was connected to Portugal.
The daughter of King Duarte of Portugal and Leonor of Aragon, she married Frederick III and was crowned Empress in Rome in 1452. Mother of Maximilian I, died in 1467.

contemporaneos.resumen: His brief reign was marked by the failure of the expedition to Tangier. He also left writings about personal government, ethics and equestrian practice.
Aljubarrota's victory secured his crown and founded the dynasty of Avis. The conquest of Ceuta during his reign opened a new stage of Portuguese expansion.

The recognized daughter of Henry IV of Castile and Juana of Portugal, she disputed the Spanish succession to Elizabeth I. She was proclaimed queen by her supporters and married Alfonso V of Portugal in 1475. After the 1479 agreements she lived in Portugal, where she died in 1530. The nickname "the Beltraneja" comes from an accusation of her paternity, not from a proven filiation.
His reign consolidated the Portuguese presence in Brazil and on the Asian routes. The introduction of the Inquisition profoundly transformed the religious and social life of the kingdom.
King of Portugal who strengthened monarchical authority against high nobility and continued Atlantic expansion. His reign prepared the great ultra-amarine leap of Manuel I.
King of Portugal involved in North African campaigns and in the dispute for the Spanish succession. His marriage to Juana la Beltraneja led him to face Isabel I and Fernando politically.

DAVID9GEO.name: David IX of Georgia
DAVID9GEO.summary: He inherited the reunification promoted by George V. His reign coincided with the Black Death and a change in regional balance after the weakening of the Iljanate. His son Bagrat V continued the royal line.

translatedSource.resumen: He inherited the reunification promoted by George V. His reign coincided with the Black Death and a change in regional balance after the weakening of the Iljanate. His son Bagrat V continued the royal line.
translatedSource.biografia: He inherited the reunification promoted by George V. His reign coincided with the Black Death and a change in regional balance after the weakening of the Iljanate. His son Bagrat V continued the royal line.

aliases: Jorge V el Brillante de Georgia
padres.resumen: He strengthened royal authority and reunited fragmented territories under Mongol domination. The recovery was gradual: numismatic evidence qualifies any image of a complete and immediate break with the Ilkhanate. He maintained relations with Italian merchants and the powers of the eastern Mediterranean.

hijos.resumen: The invasion of Tamerlán culminated in the seizure of Tbilis and his captivity in 1386. He was released, but the Western campaigns and rebellions eroded the authority he had inherited. His sons George VII and Constantine I were kings.

notas.texto: David appears with number VII as part of his trapezuntin bibliography and corresponds to his name's Georgian monarch, David IX at Atlas.

hijos.resumen: Georgian princess, took the name Eudoxia and married Manuel III. She was the mother of Alejo IV. Her file connects two Black Sea courts without attributing a territorial government to her for her status as consort.

relacionadosDinastia.resumen: He resisted the repeated expeditions of Tamerlan and ended up negotiating a submission that allowed the Christian monarchy to be preserved. The military devastation weakened the resources of the crown and promoted the autonomy of the regional authorities.

He succeeded his brother George VII. His alliance with Shirvan brought him into conflict with the Qara Qoyunlu; he was captured and executed. Several branches that later contested the Georgian monarchy descended from his children.

He reigned in eastern Georgia under the Iljanate and participated in his campaigns. His execution by order of the Khan illustrates how far the sovereignty of the Bagrationi depended on the policy of the Mongolian court.

Son of Rusudan, he shared the crown with his cousin David VII by Mongol decision. After rebelling, he consolidated his power in the west, where the division of Georgia gave rise to the Imeretian monarchy under the same dynasty.

Son of Constantine I and father of Bagrat VI. His position in genealogy allows us to understand that the branch that ended up ruling Imereti came from the Georgian royal family itself, even though it faced other descendants of that house.

His brief reign continued the restoration begun by Alexander I while his brothers exercised regional power. He died without an heir to consolidate his line; the succession opened the way to George VIII and renewed disputes among the Bagrationi.

contemporaneos.resumen: He succeeded his brother George VII. His alliance with Shirvan brought him into conflict with the Qara Qoyunlu; he was captured and executed. Several branches that later contested the Georgian monarchy descended from his children.

He resisted the repeated expeditions of Tamerlan and ended up negotiating a submission that allowed the Christian monarchy to be preserved. The military devastation weakened the resources of the crown and promoted the autonomy of the regional authorities.

Lord of Samtsje, he ruled a border between Georgia, the Mongolian world and Trebizond. The marriages of his daughters link his house with the Bagrationi and the Grand Komnenoi; his grandson George V grew up in his surroundings.
Emperor of the house of Wittelsbach whose struggle for the German crown led to a prolonged conflict with the papacy. His reign reflected the political fracture of the Holy Empire in the 14th century.

Emperor of the house of Luxembourg and king of Bohemia, became Prague one of the great political and cultural centers of Europe. The Gold Bullet of 1356 ordered the imperial election in a lasting way.
He reintegrated Mallorca into his domains and fought Pedro I of Castilla. His reign reinforced the ceremonial regio and left an important autobiographical chronicle.

BEATINGLATERRA.name: Beatrice of England
BEATINGLATERRA.summary: Consort of the Plantagenet dynasty. Their career was connected to Brittany.

translatedSource.resumen: Consort of the Plantagenet dynasty. Their career was connected to Brittany.
translatedSource.biografia: Consort of the Plantagenet dynasty. Their career was connected to Brittany.

padres.resumen: His long reign culminated in a confrontation with the barons headed by Simon de Montfort. The crisis expanded the role of representative assemblies in English politics.
Consort of the Barcelona dynasty. Their career was connected to England.

conyuges.resumen: Son of John I and White of Champagne, he married Beatriz of England. With him they combine the Breton ducal heritage, the Navarre connection of his mother and the English of his wife. His son Arthur II was the father of the lines between which the duchy would be later disputed.

hijos.resumen: The daughter of John II of Brittany and Beatrice of England, she married Philip of Artois. Her offspring linked with the Évreux through Margaret of Artois. The Brittany-Artois-Évreux chain constitutes an important family connection between the Atlantic Duchy and the Navarrese monarchy.
A son of John II and Beatrice of England, he succeeded to the duchy in 1305. He had children by his marriages to Marie of Limoges and Yolande of Dreux.
hijos.biografia: A son of John II and Beatrice of England, he succeeded to the duchy in 1305. He had children by his marriages to Marie of Limoges and Yolande of Dreux. That family division became decisive after his death: the rights of his son Guy’s descendants and those of John of Montfort fuelled the dispute over Brittany.

relacionadosDinastia.resumen: Consort of the Plantagenet dynasty. Their life was connected with England and Scotland.
King of England, Reformer of the Regy administration and protagonist of the wars in Wales and Scotland. His intervention in Scottish succession triggered a long-term conflict.
Brother of Henry III of England, he was elected King of the Romans by a part of the electors. His candidacy competed with that of Alfonso X of Castile during the imperial interregno.
Consort of the Plantagenet dynasty. Their life was connected with Holy Roman Empire and England.
Consort of the Plantagenet dynasty. Their career was connected to England, Scotland.

Daughter of Edward I and Leonor of Castile, she married John II of Brabant. She was the mother of John III. Through her, the Brabantine ducal line was connected to England and Castile before her subsequent relationship with the Valois of Burgundy.

contemporaneos.resumen: Known as Pierre Mauclerc, he belonged to Dreux's house and agreed to the Breton government for his marriage to Alix of Thouars. After her death, he exercised the regency of his son John I.

The son of Alix of Thouars and Peter of Dreux, he inherited the duchy as a child. His father exercised the government during his minority. John's marriage to Blanca de Champagne linked Brittany to the family in Navarre; his son John II continued the ducal line.
